answers.rationale: For work trips with early starts, no car, and a fixed training site, Maya repeatedly prioritizes the closest/connected hotel and reliable dinner access over included breakfast. The connected property removes morning transfer risk after her prep call; paid breakfast is appropriately disclosed rather than assumed covered by registration.

A best matches the family's established early-morning pattern: two real beds, included breakfast, kitchenette, nearby restaurants, and an easy walk after parking once. The marginally shorter walk and higher rating at B do not outweigh A's simpler Saturday morning and more useful room setup.

A preserves the family priorities for an early event: two queens, included breakfast, nearby food, and a short convention-center trip. B's slightly higher rating, larger room, and one-minute shorter drive do not justify giving up included breakfast when the practical location difference is negligible.

A is the strongest combined fit: two queens, included breakfast, mini-fridge, restaurants nearby, and a short walk to morning campus programming. The alternatives either add paid breakfast or a meaningful drive without providing enough compensating benefit.
